text:
A: Hello, hello! Gurpreet, yes?
B: Yes, hello. How are you?
A: Good, good, thank you. Abdul, from Leyton. And how are you, my friend?
B: I'm okay, thank you. I saw your photo, you have chillies on balcony, yeah?
A: Yes! You saw them! Nobody notices my chillies. Yes, few pots. This year better than last year.
B: Me also. I grow chillies and coriander, on the patio, Hayes. This year very good, too many. Simran says give to neighbours.
A: Same, same! What kind you grow?
B: Green ones, small, the hot ones. From India seeds, my cousin brought.
A: I have the Bangladeshi ones, naga, very hot. One time I put two in the fish curry, my partner Shirin, she was crying. Water, water! Now she watches me when I cook.
B: Ha! Naga, yes, very strong. I don't touch that one.
A: You cook also?
B: Little bit. Aloo parathas on my day off. And in gurdwara, langar, on gurpurab, we cook for big numbers, hundreds people.
A: Hundreds! That's proper cooking. I learned in restaurants, Brick Lane, long time ago. Big pots, big fire. Now I do Sunday dinner for the family, my stepson comes, Rayhan. He eats like three people.
B: Young boys, yeah, yeah. Always hungry.
A: Always. What you do for work, Gurpreet?
B: Food factory near Heathrow. Tray-sealing. Part-time, because my back.
A: Ah, back. Sorry to hear. I'm a porter, hospital, Whitechapel, I see lots of backs. Lot of porters, we have problem with back, knees. My knees, they're starting now. What happened to yours?
B: Lifting, the film rolls. Two years ago. It's okay now, little bit hard sometimes. I walk, Lake Farm, slowly.
A: Walking is the best. Doctors always tell this. Slowly, slowly, but every day.
B: Yes. Physio said same. You are walking a lot in the hospital, innit?
A: Twenty thousand steps! I told Hitesh before, the hospital is my gym. He said he bowls fast. I didn't argue with him.
B: Ha. I talked to Nilesh before you, he does same job as me. Same machine.
A: Nilesh, yes, nice man, quiet. I spoke to him first. He looks after his dad. Good boy.
B: Yeah, he seems very good. My parents are in Punjab. I call my mum every evening, video call.
A: Every evening, that's very good. My father, er, he passed when I was here, so... call your mum. Every evening, keep doing it.
B: Yeah. I will. Sorry about your father.
A: Thank you. Long time now. You go back to Punjab sometimes?
B: Every two years, in winter. But flights to Amritsar now, so expensive, every year going up.
A: Sylhet same! I look at the price, I close the laptop, I open it again next day, maybe it's cheaper. Never cheaper.
B: Never, yeah, yeah. Same with the cash and carry, everything—
